tool_input.title: shop/api CrashLoopBackOff - REDIS_HOST service name mismatch
tool_input.content:
On 2026-10-02, the `api` Deployment in namespace `shop` (cluster aurora-lab / kind-aurora-lab, kubeconfig-ee1ed628176351ce) rolled out revision 2 with `REDIS_HOST=redis-master`, but the actual Kubernetes Service in that namespace is named `redis` (ClusterIP 10.96.111.208, port 6379) — there is no `redis-master` Service. New pods (ReplicaSet api-869d87b484) crash-looped with exit code 1; `kubectl logs --previous` showed `redis connection failed... [Errno -2] Name does not resolve` x5 then `giving up: redis unavailable`. The old ReplicaSet (api-f64486c4c) with `REDIS_HOST=redis` kept running fine, so the rollout stalled at unavailableReplicas=1 instead of fully failing — service stayed up via old pods during the incident.

**Why:** A deploy changed an env var to reference a service name that doesn't exist/match. Classic deploy-introduced config drift, not a resource or infra problem. CPU/memory were trivial (<15Mi used out of 128Mi limit) and all 3 nodes were Ready — ruled out resource exhaustion and node issues.

**How to apply:** When `KubePodCrashLooping` fires for `shop`/`api` (or similar) right after a deploy:
1. `kubectl get rs -n shop -o wide` to see if there's a new vs old ReplicaSet (deploy stuck mid-rollout).
2. `kubectl logs <crashing-pod> -n shop --previous` for the real app error.
3. `kubectl get svc -n shop` and diff env vars between old (working) and new (crashing) pod specs — look for host/service name mismatches.
4. Fix: correct the env var to the real service name (`kubectl set env deployment/api -n shop REDIS_HOST=redis`) or `kubectl rollout undo deployment/api -n shop` to roll back to the last-good revision.
